title: Adaptive kernel entrainment for mixed FlashAttn v2/v3 workloads and cold-path alignment
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Problem: We observe intermittent latency regressions and increased startup latency on mixed-tenant fleets that serve both FlashAttn v2 and v3 model variants. The runtime's current kernel selector sometimes oscillates during cold-paths (first few requests after idle), causing repeated kernel handoffs, workspace reallocations, and decode jitter. This ticket scopes an adaptive 'entrainment' approach that smooths kernel selection during cold starts, aligns prefill/decode pacing with expected KV cache warmup, and provides a simulated cold-path testing harness to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start 95th-percentile latency reduced by >=20% for mixed v2/v3 traffic in synthetic replay tests
Kernel handoff rate during first 30s of idle-replay reduced to <5% of requests in canary cluster
No >2% regression in steady-state median latency across benchmark suites
Canary rollout automation with automatic rollback on SLO breach implemented
tasks: Instrument selector with per-tenant cold-start affinity and recent-success score
Design an entrainment window heuristic: keep initial kernel choice for N first decodes unless high error/oom observed
Implement a lightweight simulated-coldstart harness that replays idle-to-burst traces against kernel selector logic
Add telemetry counters: kernel_handoff, handoff_reason, workspace_reallocs, prefill_kv_hits, latency_breakdown
Create canary gating: metric thresholds and automated rollback playbook
Run cross-precision replay (fp16/quant) to validate no precision-induced handoffs
Prepare load test with mixed v2/v3 model shapes and long-context scenarios
telemetry_queries: SELECT p95(latency) FROM serving.requests WHERE time > now() - 1h AND kernel_variant IN ('fa2','fa3') GROUP BY tenant
COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE kernel_handoff=true) BY kernel_variant, tenant, minute
SUM(prefill_kv_hits) / SUM(prefill_requests) AS kv_hit_rate BY tenant, hour
rollout_plan: staging: enable entrainment flag for 10% of capacity with synthetic trace replay
canary: route 1% of production traffic (non-critical tenants) for 24h with automatic SLO checks
gradual: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with staggered tenant cohorts and rollback gates
monitor: 48h post-100% watch with regression alerting and quick rollback runbook
risks: Too-conservative entrainment can delay beneficial kernel upgrades for long-running sessions
Entrained selection may increase cost if a suboptimal kernel is kept for long bursts
Edge cases: sudden model shape changes mid-request could still trigger reallocations
Telemetry skew may hide regressions for low-volume tenants
